5

Everyday / Sports · c. 36–42.5mm · 30m, 50m, 100m · automatic · 1976–2026

The Seiko 5 is a line of affordable, durable, and reliable automatic watches first introduced in 1963. It is defined by five core attributes: an automatic movement, a day-date display in a single window, water resistance, a recessed crown at 4 o'clock, and a robust case and bracelet.

The story

The Seiko 5 was introduced in 1963 with the Sportsmatic 5, designed to be a practical and accessible mechanical watch for the growing youth market of the 1960s. Its five key features and reliable performance led to immense popularity, with exports in 1966 reportedly surpassing the total number of automatic watches produced in Switzerland. Over the decades, the Seiko 5 line has been powered by a series of robust, workhorse movements, evolving from the 6619 and 7009 calibers of the 60s and 70s to the long-running 7S26 introduced in 1996. In recent years, the collection has been updated with the 4R36 caliber, which adds modern features like hacking and hand-winding, continuing the family's legacy of providing high-value mechanical watchmaking to a wide audience.
